tools.name: grant_coach_access_to_athlete
tools.description: Gives a coach access to an athlete's training log by adding the coach to the athlete's access list with the chosen permission level (view or edit).

params.name: athlete_id
params.description: ID of the athlete who owns the training log

params.name: coach_id
params.description: ID of the coach receiving access

tools.code:
import sqlite3
from langchain_core.tools import tool

DATABASE_PATH = "fitness.db"


@tool
def grant_coach_access_to_athlete(athlete_id: int, coach_id: int, permission_level: str) -> str:
    database_connection = sqlite3.connect(DATABASE_PATH)
    normalized_permission_level = permission_level.strip().lower()
    if normalized_permission_level not in ("view", "edit"):
        database_connection.close()
        return "Invalid permission level"
    database_connection.execute(
        "INSERT INTO athlete_access (athlete_id, coach_id, permission_level) VALUES (?, ?, ?) "
        "ON CONFLICT(athlete_id, coach_id) DO UPDATE SET permission_level = excluded.permission_level",
        (athlete_id, coach_id, normalized_permission_level),
    )
    database_connection.commit()
    database_connection.close()
    return f"Coach {coach_id} now has {normalized_permission_level} access to athlete {athlete_id}"

tools.name: archive_and_upload_workout_export
tools.description: Moves a workout export file into the archive folder, then uploads the archived copy to the user's cloud backup bucket.

params.name: export_file_path
params.description: Path to the workout export file

params.name: archive_directory
params.description: Local directory where the file is moved

params.name: bucket_name
params.description: Name of the S3 backup bucket

params.name: user_id
params.description: ID of the user whose workouts are exported

tools.code:
import shutil
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import boto3
from langchain_core.tools import tool

s3_client = boto3.client("s3")


@tool
def archive_and_upload_workout_export(export_file_path: str, archive_directory: str, bucket_name: str, user_id: str) -> dict:
    source_path = Path(export_file_path)
    archive_path = Path(archive_directory)
    archive_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    timestamp_text = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ")
    archived_file_name = f"{timestamp_text}_{source_path.name}"
    destination_path = archive_path / archived_file_name
    shutil.move(str(source_path), str(destination_path))
    object_key = f"users/{user_id}/workout_exports/{archived_file_name}"
    file_size_bytes = destination_path.stat().st_size
    s3_client.upload_file(
        Filename=str(destination_path),
        Bucket=bucket_name,
        Key=object_key,
        ExtraArgs={"ServerSideEncryption": "AES256"},
    )
    return {
        "archived_path": str(destination_path),
        "bucket": bucket_name,
        "key": object_key,
        "size_bytes": file_size_bytes,
    }

tools.name: get_weekly_workout_totals
tools.description: Looks up a user's total workout count, minutes, and calories burned for the 7 days starting at the given date.
tools.code:
import sqlite3

DATABASE_PATH = "fitness.db"


def get_weekly_workout_totals(user_id: int, week_start_date: str) -> dict:
    database_connection = sqlite3.connect(DATABASE_PATH)
    weekly_totals_row = database_connection.execute(
        "SELECT COUNT(*), COALESCE(SUM(duration_minutes), 0), COALESCE(SUM(calories_burned), 0) "
        "FROM workouts WHERE user_id = ? AND workout_date >= ? AND workout_date < date(?, '+7 days')",
        (user_id, week_start_date, week_start_date),
    ).fetchone()
    database_connection.close()
    return {
        "workout_count": weekly_totals_row[0],
        "total_minutes": weekly_totals_row[1],
        "total_calories": weekly_totals_row[2],
    }
